source_metadata.exact_title: Prevalence of Clinically Significant Drug-Drug Interactions Across US Children’s Hospitals
source_metadata.citation: Antoon JW, Hall M, Herndon A, et al. Pediatrics. 2020;146(5):e20200858.
source_metadata.study_design: Multicenter retrospective cohort study using PHIS

duplicate_review.note: Deterministic unique atom IDs were generated per extracted assertion; no duplicate source-row assertions were intentionally merged.

consistency_findings.issue: Study period wording is internally inconsistent: Methods specify Jan 1, 2016 through Dec 31, 2018 (36 months), while Results/Discussion refer to a “2-year study period.” No correction was imposed.

Methods describe adjusted hospital proportions using a generalized linear mixed-effects model with hospital as a random effect, whereas the Figure 1 caption describes adjusted proportions as derived by multivariable logistic regression. The source wording was preserved rather than reconciled.

extraction_limitations: Atoms represent assertions in the primary article; cited external-study results in the introduction/discussion were not re-extracted as primary-study evidence.
The article defines DDI exposure as same-day administration; the ATOM set does not infer clinical harm, preventability, or pharmacokinetic overlap from that definition.

Table 3 rates reported as <0.01 per 1000 days cannot be represented exactly by the quantitative_result numeric estimate field; for those rows the atom quantifies directly reported patient-days and preserves the <0.01 rate in the canonical statement/original_result_text.
Drug-class/mechanism “+” markers in Table 3 were normalized to base drug names in ConceptRef text; the source method defining class/mechanism expansion is captured separately.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated field for inequality-valued quantitative estimates such as <0.01.
The schema has no dedicated study-level metadata object; source metadata is therefore provided in this validation report rather than repeated in every atom.
The schema does not distinguish exposure prevalence from actual DDI-related adverse events; the extraction preserves the article’s exposure endpoint and does not treat it as harm.
